verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas documents a first-party Editor API for automating and extending the Editor: scene manipulation, asset management and custom tool integration. It also offers an official Editor MCP Server that modifies project data in an open Editor session, and PCUI, the UI library the Editor is built with, for building browser-based tools. missing for 10: a documented plugin packaging/loading mechanism, independent or hands-on corroboration of Editor API depth beyond vendor docs.

support.subject: As a game developer, I can extend and automate the editor itself — custom tools, editor scripts, plugins that manipulate scenes and assets programmatically

citations.quote: The Editor module provides a comprehensive API for automating and extending the functionality of the PlayCanvas Editor. It allows developers to programmatically interact with the Editor, facilitating tasks such as scene manipulation, asset management, and custom tool integration.
This module is essential for developers looking to streamline their workflow, create custom editing tools, or integrate external data and systems into the PlayCanvas Editor environment.
change scenes from code with the Editor API, or from an agent with the MCP server.
It can modify project data and verify the result through the viewport or a running application.
PCUI (`@playcanvas/pcui`) is the UI component library the PlayCanvas Editor is built with, for building browser-based tools, with React wrappers.
